text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
POLITIKA
- Yugoslavia's Supreme Defence council positvely assesses the army's combat readiness and stresses necessity to secure financing of the army from real sources in 1997.
- Croatian Foreign Minister Mate Granic visits Belgrade to continue talks on normalisation of relations between the two countries.

- There should be continued international monitoring in the region of eastern Slavonia after its reintegration into Croatia to give a feeling of security to the local population, says U.N Human rights rapporteur Elisabeth Rehn in Vukovar.
- Latest developments have slowed down talks with the International Monetary Fund, said Yugoslav minister for science and development Janko Radulovic.
- Yugoslavia should pay gas and oil imported under its barter deal with highly processed goods, says president of the Yugoslav Chamber of Commerce Mihajlo Milojevic.
- Second Balkan cardiologists' conference to be held in Belgrade on March 29.
- Striking teachers reject agreement signed by prime minister and president of the trade union confederation and reduce their demands for a wage increase to 43 percent from around 100 percent.
- Terrorist attacks are becoming part of everyday life, says commentary following explosion in the house of singer and member of Yugoslav Left leadership Zorica Brunclik.
- Democratic Party president Zoran Djindjic and Serbian Renewal Party Belgrade head Spasoje Krunic have the best chance of becoming the new Belgrade mayor and head of city government.
NASA BORBA
- Student protests continue. A car drives into the students, hurts four and has its windows smashed.
- Serbian Education Minister Jovan Todorovic promises students the university rector will leave when they return to class, the students want it to happen the other way round.
- Two day Forum for Kosovo to be held in Vienna on April 19 and 20.
- Foundry workers at Belgrade's motor and tractor factory IMT are on strike demanding several months' outstanding wages and restarting of production.
- Citizens of Nis hold final protest rally over local electoral fraud, the new mayor thanks them for having completed an important job.
BORBA

- Yugoslav society needs a concept of material and spiritual renewal following a dramatic period the country has gone through, says president of the directorate of the Yugoslav left (JUL) Mira Markovic in an interview.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI

- Yugoslav delegation to bilateral talks on the succession of the former Yugoslavia does not accept the division of the former federation's archives saying this would scatter the testimony of more than 70 years of a state's history.
-- Belgrade newsroom, 381 11 222 4305
